items.title: 68728_Jonah
items.q: there was Lamarr and Brownie [Andrew Brown] He was the third alto player.

ctx.x: He played sort of an arranger's piano, didn't he? I mean he didn't play --

Yeah, not too much of a soloist, you know. Just arranger's piano. Maybe you'll see him in that picture, "Sensations of '44," where they've got one piano over there, another one over there. One's Dave Rivera and one is Buster. That's when Illinois Jacquet was in the band. See, when Chu died, we tried to get a tenor player, so we got Mac Rae, who was going to Canada, and when Chu got killed coming out of Youngstown. He was going to the Peace Bridge, going to Canada. I'll never forget that night. See, and they used…

and Cab said, "Man, there was an accident up there. Now I guess we'll be held up here for who can tell how long," not thinking it was them, you know. And the closer we got up on them -- because Cab always rode up front, and he said, "Man, that looks like Chu laying out there," you know. And he says it is. We stopped the bus and all of us jumped out, and we got him, you know, picked him up. He was laying there. His head was bashed in back here on the side. And his pipe was broken in about three places. And Brownie…
